notes: No live divyam binary/server in-session, so runs are graded on command-string correctness and behavior (hand-off, confirmation, dashboard links, traffic math), not live execution.

evals.name: add-gemini-model-handoff
evals.prompt: add a model gemini 2.5 flash from google with the gemini endpoint, api key is AIzaSyEXAMPLE1234567890
evals.expected_output: Builds a `divyam model-info create --provider-name google --api-type GEMINI --model-names gemini-2.5-flash --provider-base-url ""` command with --provider-api-key as a bare (value-less) interactive flag. Does NOT run it and does NOT echo the key back. Tells the user to run it in their terminal where it prompts for the key.

assertions.text: Uses `model-info create` with --api-type GEMINI and provider google
Model name is gemini-2.5-flash
--provider-api-key is a bare flag (no value on the command line)
Does not print/echo the AIza... key value back
Hands the command to the user to run rather than executing it

evals.name: add-another-bedrock-with-prices
evals.prompt: now add another model with the same details but it's claude sonnet on aws bedrock, input price is 3 and output is 15 dollars per million tokens
evals.expected_output: Reuses the prior model-info create shape, switches provider to bedrock and api-type to COMPLETIONS, adds --input-price 3 --output-price 15 (per 1,000,000 tokens, USD). Still hands off with --provider-api-key as a bare flag if a key is needed.

assertions.text: Provider switched to bedrock (not google)
Includes --input-price 3 and --output-price 15
Does not reuse the Gemini GEMINI api-type for a Bedrock chat model
Reuses/acknowledges the previous command shape rather than starting from scratch

evals.name: create-selector-then-prod
evals.prompt: create a selector called checkout-router using the default extractor over the last 30 days, then move it to prod
evals.expected_output: Runs `selector create --name checkout-router -x <extractor>` (no timestamps needed for last-30-days default), then emits the Selector Training dashboard link with the SA to filter on. For the prod move, prints `selector update --id <id> --to-prod` and asks for confirmation before running.

assertions.text: selector create includes --name checkout-router and an extractor strategy (-x)
Emits the Selector Training dashboard URL (training-dashboard) after creation
For --to-prod, asks for explicit confirmation before running
Does not silently promote to prod

evals.name: allocate-traffic-rebalance
evals.prompt: allocate 20% traffic to the checkout-router selector. current allocation is control 10, selector_disabled 90
evals.expected_output: Reads current allocation, computes a new map with the selector bucket at 20, control kept >= ~2, total 100 (e.g. control 8, selector_disabled 72, checkout-router 20), shows before->after, and asks for confirmation before `sa update --traffic-allocation-config`.

assertions.text: New allocation sums to exactly 100
checkout-router bucket is set to 20
control stays at or above ~1-2%
Shows before->after and asks for confirmation before applying
Uses sa update --traffic-allocation-config to apply

evals.name: sa-cost-efficient
evals.prompt: make this service account cost efficient
evals.expected_output: Runs `divyam sa update --optimization-goal COST_EFFICIENT` (the SA optimization goal), not a selector lambda change.

assertions.text: Uses sa update --optimization-goal COST_EFFICIENT
Does not confuse this with selector --cost-savings-lambda

evals.name: rotate-api-key
evals.prompt: rotate the api key for this service account
evals.expected_output: Runs `sa key create --name <n>`, surfaces the one-time api_key with a save-now/unrecoverable warning, offers to persist it via `config set ... --api-token` (bare interactive) + `config use`, and flags revoking the old key (`sa key revoke --key-id`) as a confirmed follow-up. Never writes the key to disk on its own.

assertions.text: Uses sa key create to make the new key
Warns the api_key is shown once / unrecoverable
Offers to persist via config set with --api-token as a bare interactive flag
Treats revoking the old key as a confirmed follow-up, keeping one active key
